description.sr_latin: Kako da kažeš šta misliš i kako se osećaš — bez filtera.
description.en: How to say what you think and how you feel — unfiltered.

phrases.context: Standard way to agree with someone's point.
phrases.notes: Reflexive verb — the 'se' is mandatory.

phrases.context: Quick confirmation, like nodding along emphatically.
Stronger emphasis than just 'tačno' — you fully back what was said.
phrases.notes: 'Baš' is an intensifier you'll hear constantly. It means 'really/exactly/just'.

phrases.context: Telling someone they're correct. Works in arguments too when you're conceding.
Dismissive disagreement. Like waving something off as ridiculous.
phrases.notes: Very common in casual speech. Tone matters — can be lighthearted or firm.

phrases.context: Softer disagreement — you're correcting without starting a fight.
Direct but not aggressive. Fine for normal conversation.
When someone says something you think is nonsense. Eye-roll energy.
phrases.notes: 'Ma daj' on its own is already a classic dismissal.

phrases.context: The go-to reaction for surprise. Use it constantly.
phrases.notes: Also works as a statement: 'Stvarno.' = 'For real.'

phrases.context: Genuine shock or disbelief. Also used sarcastically.
Slightly more intense than 'stvarno' — you're checking if they're joking.
Exasperated acceptance. You don't love it but you'll deal.
phrases.notes: Tone is everything. Can range from mild annoyance to barely contained rage.

phrases.en: It's annoying me. / It's boring me.
phrases.context: Something or someone is getting on your nerves or boring you to death.
phrases.notes: 'Smaranje' (noun) = annoyance/boredom. Very common casual word.

phrases.en: I can't anymore. / I've had enough.
phrases.context: You're done. Fed up. Over it. Works for anything from a bad day to a long meeting.
Straightforward — something is getting under your skin.
Pure enthusiasm. Good news, great food, anything positive.

phrases.en: I'm really glad. / That makes me really happy.
phrases.context: Genuine warmth. Use when hearing good news about someone you care about.
Excited anticipation — a trip, seeing someone, an event.
phrases.notes: Literally 'I barely wait.' Natural and very common.

phrases.context: Dripping sarcasm when someone states the obvious.
phrases.notes: Literally 'Don't!' but used purely sarcastically in this context.

phrases.context: Can be genuine praise OR devastating sarcasm depending on tone. Context is king.
phrases.notes: Literally 'every honor.' One of the most versatile Serbian expressions.

phrases.context: Almost always sarcastic. When someone does or says something dumb.
phrases.notes: For a female target: 'Baš si pametna.' Adjective changes by gender.

phrases.context: Casual approval. Yes, they use 'kul' borrowed from English.
phrases.notes: Also hear 'ekstra' or 'do jaja' for cool/awesome (the latter is vulgar but very common).

phrases.context: When something is tediously dull. Very casual.
phrases.notes: From 'smoriti se' — to get bored/fed up.

phrases.en: It kills my vibe. / It's mind-numbing.
phrases.context: Something is so boring or annoying it's draining your life force.
phrases.notes: Literally 'kills me into concept.' A very expressive, very Serbian complaint.

phrases.context: Something is impressively cool. Slightly retro slang but still used.
phrases.notes: Literally means 'horror/dread' — used positively, like English 'sick' or 'wicked'.

phrases.context: Reacting to bad news, a terrible situation, or something awful.
phrases.notes: Literally 'horror.' Can also be used for dramatic effect over minor things.

phrases.context: Seeing something adorable — a baby, a puppy, or your girlfriend doing something cute.
Big happiness — engagement, promotion, great news.
phrases.notes: Female speaker: 'Presrećna sam.' The prefix 'pre-' intensifies the adjective.

phrases.context: Venting about someone who got under your skin.
phrases.notes: Change ending for gender: 'iznervirala' (she), 'iznerviralo' (it/situation).

phrases.context: General approval — food, a movie, an idea, anything.
phrases.notes: Emphasizing 'meni' (to me) is optional but natural in conversation.

phrases.context: Polite-ish way to say you're not impressed. Very understated.
phrases.notes: Literally 'It's not something to me.' Perfectly diplomatic.

phrases.en: In my opinion, that makes no sense.
phrases.context: Starting a sentence with your take. 'Po meni' = 'according to me.'
You could not care less. Casual and slightly blunt.
phrases.notes: Literally 'my ear hurts.' There's a vulgar version with a different body part that's even more common.

phrases.en: I'm not so sure about that.
phrases.context: You have doubts but don't want to be confrontational.
Halfway conceding. You're not fully convinced but you'll give ground.
Stalling before delivering an opinion you know they won't love.
phrases.notes: Classic hedge. Everyone will recognize you're about to say something uncomfortable.
